planned.paragraphMeaning: The chapter opens on a late-July afternoon beside the old canal in Funaki, where the family’s calligraphy school and its wooden sign stand among traditional tiled-roof homes.
planned.sceneDescription: A quiet establishing view of the Japanese canal town Funaki: tied wooden boats, dark tiled-roof houses and the Takagi calligraphy school with a simple blank wooden signboard, in warm late-July afternoon light.

planned.paragraphMeaning: Mio removes the “Closed Today” sign from the classroom door; a white envelope drops to her feet, carrying her grandfather’s first clue.
planned.sceneDescription: Inside the quiet tatami calligraphy school, Mio lifts a completely blank wooden sign from its hook as a small white envelope lies freshly fallen on the floor beside her; the envelope and sign have no writing.

planned.paragraphMeaning: At night Mio discovers the classroom drawers emptied and blank papers scattered; a face-hidden figure with a black umbrella slips through the garden gate.
planned.sceneDescription: Mio stands in the dark classroom beside an open desk with seven pulled-out drawers and blank sheets scattered across tatami, looking through the garden-facing glass door at a face-hidden black-umbrella silhouette leaving through the gate into night.
